proposed_english: to reckon / to set / to establish (commemorative)
rationale: Recurring verb on this page (lines 4, 6, 11, 12, 26) in the technical sense of establishing/reckoning a rest or remembrance for a departed catechumen. Likely a Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' with prosthetic ϩⲉⲓ-. Functions both intransitively ('be reckoned to') and transitively ('reckon X for Y'). Distinct from ⲣ̄-ⲡⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'make remembrance' (already in glossary) — possibly its semantic neighbor in the cultic-commemorative register.

Hapax in this corpus (line 3). Two candidate analyses: (a) Lyc. for ⲥⲁⲡⲥⲡ̄ 'petition, supplication' fitting the ecclesiastical intercession-context; (b) Lyc. for ⲥⲱⲡⲧ̄/ⲥⲁⲃⲧⲉ 'preparation, fitting thing,' the church's ritual provision for the dead. Confidence low.

Manuscript glyph ⲋ apparently functions as variant for ϭ. ⲋⲣⲟ = ϭⲣⲟ likely an unusual Lycopolitan/Manichaean form of ⲣⲟ 'gate.' Used three times: line 7 'his four great gates,' line 17 'third gate' (section-header). Structural-enumerative use confirms the gate sense for soteriological 'gates' through which catechumens pass after death.

Lycopolitan possessive ⲡⲉϩ- 'his' + ϩⲧⲁⲩ 'four' (cf. accumulated ⲡϩⲧⲁⲩ 'the four'). The doubled ϩ reflects assimilation of the possessive-prefix to the numeral-onset. Used here in 'his four great gates' framing the kephalaion's structural enumeration.

Lycopolitan rendering of Greek συγγενής 'kinsman, relative' with possessive prefix ⲡⲉϩ-. Lyc. ⲥⲟⲗⲧⲉⲛⲏⲥ for ⲥⲩⲅⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ — ⲗ for double-γ and ⲧ for κ. Used in the kinship-list (father/mother/son/daughter/kinsman) for whom the surviving relation makes commemoration.
Reading uncertain. Possibly Lyc. ⲡⲁⲥ = ⲡⲁⲥⲉ 'half, share, portion' — 'for the portion of the man.' Alternative: scribal/dialectal pronominal form. Recurs once on this page (line 12).
